cells.tense: The whole pattern is in front of you and you are the one holding it.
cells.ask: Write down the full version of the decision you have been carrying as separate pieces, then hand the page to one person who should see it.
cells.core: You can hold the whole thing at once. Not just your own corner of it — the moving parts, what each person wants, how it all fits. You're in it and looking at it at the same time, which is harder than either one alone. What you gather stays gathered. The pieces don't come apart when you set it down, and when you hand it to someone they get the whole shape instead of a corner. Your sense of what's fair doesn't need working out; it arrives, and it arrives clean. You see the pattern, you can say where it bends, and the saying is not a strain. Keep that moving both ways. Tell one person what's right here and let their answer land whole.
cells.sheetLine: You see the whole pattern and you hold it steady.
cells.verb: gathering scattered thoughts into one alignment
cells.place: perceiving the whole pattern from inside it

cells.tense: You are trying to settle the whole thing before anyone has said a word.
cells.ask: Before you touch the situation, sit and say what you feel about it first, then wait a day before acting.
cells.core: The picture is being assembled ahead of the moment it belongs to. You map the reactions before they come, you build the version where it is already resolved, and the gathering turns into a forecast. What you see is what might happen, not what's here, so nothing gets to land as itself. When this sits well, you gather what is actually in front of you and stop there, and your sense of what's fair can name the right thing without rehearsing it. It isn't doing that now. Steady it by starting from what you feel, then let the open thing stay open one more day. The gathering can wait until something real is there to gather.
cells.sheetLine: You settled the whole pattern before anyone spoke.

cells.tense: You stopped saying what you saw, and you still haven't stepped back inside.
cells.ask: Take one thing you see clearly across a situation and write it down for one person, saying it badly is fine.
cells.core: You can still see how it fits. The pieces land, the links show up, and none of it gets said out loud. What you notice stays inside, and the people around the situation get the corner view while you hold the whole one. Working well, you say what you see, someone hears it, and what you saw does its work by reaching them. That is the part that stopped. Say the whole thing to one person today. Write what you see about one situation and put it in front of them; it doesn't need to be tidy or certain. Say what you feel is fair while you say it, because that part is still there.
cells.sheetLine: You see it clearly and you stopped saying so.

cells.tense: You are reading the whole pattern and calling it just the shape of things.
cells.ask: Name one thing you have seen clearly about a group you're part of, then say what it means for the people in it.
cells.core: You're reading what's around you and handing it off as if it were reading itself. The pieces meet, you see where, and the fairness of it lands without being worked out — and you talk like that just happens. It doesn't; you're doing it, in the rooms you are actually in. Done right, you say the whole shape out loud and you say it as yours. The pattern is already in your hands, and the people it concerns would get it clearer if you claimed it. Say it's yours, then say what it means for them, out loud, once.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the person was ever in a room where saying what they saw across all layers did not go well — the record says the seat is starved, not what emptied it. A reader could rightly say recognition still runs in some rooms and not others, and my read flattens that. The ask survives being wrong because it only asks for one recital, and if the read is off they still end with a whole seeing written in their own words. The sentence that serves me more than them is any version of 'somewhere back there a room where it didn't go well' — the kernel has no room, so none goes in.
